newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Templeton content to hold current NZ equities.
newsitem.headline: Templeton content to hold current NZ equities.

text.p: U.S. fund manager Templeton Investments Counsel Inc is content to hold its substantial New Zealand equity assets but is not looking to accumulate more, Vice President Howard Leonard said on Wednesday.
Leonard, speaking to journalists after addressing the New Zealand Investment Conference, said the decision not to increase was more of a weighting issue.
"We are very content to hold. We think the companies are well-managed. We think they are good holdings but in most cases we are not looking to add," Leonard said.
Significant investment stopped around two years ago when the value of its rapidly appreciating investments started to exceed the appropriate weighting in its total portfolio.

It had taken a large position in Carter Holt Harvey and the price doubled. "That was the the only reason we trimmed it. As it gets above 3.0 percent, prudent portfolio management suggests you start trimming it down," he said.

On a general tack, most of New Zealand's economic indicators were positive for the country, but the current account deficit, largely forecast to widen over the next two years, was "one hole in the perfect New Zealand story".
Fort Lauderdale-based Templeton is owned by Franklin Resources. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746
